Theme

Latin word

externus

externus, externa, externum

adjective

external, outward; foreign; foreign: of another country, as against ours

In this lexicon

  • external

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.26: externus et adventīcius tepor (Lewis & Short); Cic. Ac. 2.4: illa externa, “outward goods” (Lewis & Short)

  • foreign

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 2.64: apud externōs populōs; Traupman 318: foreign (of another country)

Examples

  • nōs autem illa externa cum multīs: haec interiōra cum paucīs ex ipsō saepe cognōvimus

    but those outward things we often learned from him with many others, these inner ones with fewCic. Ac. 2.4 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for external

  • verba aut Latīna aut peregrīna sunt. Peregrīna porrō ex omnibus prope dīxerim gentibus ut hominēs, ut īnstitūta etiam multa vēnērunt.

    Words are either Latin or foreign. And foreign words have come to us, I would almost say, from every nation, as people have, and many customs too.Quint. 1.5.55
